newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX dips 0.66 pts led by Slovnaft.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX dips 0.66 pts led by Slovnaft.

text.p: Slovakia's Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) opened the week on a downward note in moderate trading on Monday, with the 16-share SAX index pulled down by oil refinery Slovnaft.
The SAX index eased 0.66 points to close at 168.59.
Slovnaft, the most heavily-weighted issue in the index, decreased by 22 crowns to 840, on volume of only 30 shares.
A new division of markets on the BSE, which became effective in August 1, appeared to have had no immediate effect on trading, though brokers hope it should increase transparency.
Turnover of 273 million crowns was made in direct trading, while only some 3.7 million crowns was generated on the automated system.
Steel maker VSZ, the most liquid first-tier issue, rose four crowns to 650, trading an unimpressive volume of 240 shares.
Trading on the listed floor was dominated by plastic pipes maker Plastika, which firmed 12 crowns to 630, trading 5,180 shares.
Overall, volume decreased to 703,358 shares, from 1.092 million shares traded on Friday, while turnover fell to 277.1 million crowns, from 783.96 million.
